newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed to firm, data loom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed to firm, data loom.

text.p: U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed to higher on Wednesday, boosted by yesterday's rally on Wall Street in cautious activity before a batch of U.S. economic reports, dealers said.
The Dow, which ended 53 points higher at 8,174.53, was seen five to 10 points firmer. At 1042 GMT, the September S&P futures contract was up 1.70 points at 948.70 on GLOBEX.

"If the bond market takes heart around midday for us and with the FTSE looking better, the Dow should be slightly better," one trader said. "But we have home sales data today and it is a huge week economically."
The September long bond was trading 4/32 higher on GLOBEX at 116-2/32. The yield on the U.S. 30-year bond ended yesterday at 6.38, its lowest since early December.
In London activity, shares in Boeing Co edged up slightly from its close of $58-9/16, after the European Commission formally cleared its merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Traders said the decision was expected, but still sparked some buying interest in Boeing.
Shares in Apple Computer Inc gained 3/8 to $16-7/8 on hopes for a strong successsor to Gilbert Amelio at the struggling personal computer company, traders said.

Amelio, the former chairman and chief executive who resigned three weeks ago, said on Tuesday he had "no clue" whom Apple was considering to replace him. He said he did not know if Steven Jobs, the company's co-founder and part-time advisor, was interested.
Dell Computer stock extended its gains from New York, rising 1/2 to $81-3/8, and International Business Machines Corp, recovering from a selloff, traded 1/4 to $103-1/8.

On the U.S. economic front, new homes sales were expected to decline to an annualized rate of 818,000 in June from 825,000 in May, according to a Reuter survey. The report is due at 1400 GMT on Wednesday.
The week's top data are U.S. unemployment and non-farm payrolls for July, to be released on Friday.
